title: Punt FG%: Player Targets
brief: Which players fit a punt FG% build, tiered by value, with their volume in PTS, 3PTM and AST? It must explain why FG% swings week to week and why punting one percentage category works well in head-to-head.
summary: FG% swings more from week to week than any other category, so in our 9-cat head-to-head league it is the cheapest category to give up. A punt FG% team gives up FG% every week and builds to win at least 5 of the other 8 categories. Target high-volume guards and forwards who bring threes, points, assists and FT% but shoot poorly, and buy them at the discount their FG% creates.

sections.heading: Why FG% swings week to week

paragraphs.text: FG% changes a lot from game to game. One note says it is the percentage category that varies most from game to game and week to week. FT% is different: it varies most from one year to the next.
Low-volume weeks make this worse. With fewer attempts, each miss moves the percentage more. A week with few games, or with stars resting, can flip FG% no matter how your roster was built.

In head-to-head, efficiency is the category that changes most from week to week. One expert prefers steady volume to a small efficiency edge for that reason. Good efficiency on low volume does not matter much either, because FG% in our league is total makes over total attempts.

sections.heading: Why punting one percentage works in H2H

paragraphs.text: Each week you win or lose 9 categories against one opponent, so 5 wins take the week. Punting FG% means you give up FG% every week and aim for at least 5 of the other 8. Because FG% swings so much week to week, a category you could only win some weeks costs little to give up.

Being strong in both FG% and FT% is very hard. If you barely win both, that lead is fragile, and paying for it leaves you short in other categories. Pick one percentage to chase. In a punt FG% build that means FT%, along with threes, points, assists and steals.

Players with outlier FG% tend to regress, and a small drop can wipe out most of their edge. A punt FG% team does not need those players at all. Leave them to balanced managers and spend that money on volume.

sections.heading: How to run it in our auction

paragraphs.text: On 2026-10-18, spend your main money on the core tier. These are high-usage guards and forwards whose only real flaw is FG%, sometimes with turnovers. Many of them also fit a punt TO build, so you can give up both categories and still aim for 5 of the remaining 7. Do not repeat last season's prices for players our league overpaid. Several of them now cost much less on Yahoo.

Save money for the end of the draft. Many poor-shooting players who add threes, assists, steals or blocks are ranked near the edge of our 144-player pool. They are 1 to 2 USD picks at the end, not mid-round buys. Others sit outside the 144 and belong on your FAB watch list instead.

Do not take FT% for granted. FT% varies most from year to year, so a player's FT% last season does not guarantee the same this season. Check your team FT% in the first two weeks. If it is slipping, use trades or FAB to fix it before the 2027-03-04 deadline.

The notes do not disagree on this strategy. They all favour steady volume over a small efficiency edge. One caution remains. The same note that makes FG% the best category to punt also says FT% is the least stable from year to year. So a punt FG% team relies on its least stable category from year to year.

Our playoffs are weeks 19 to 21 and end 2027-03-28. Short weeks make percentages more random, but that hurts a punt FG% team less, because FG% is already given up. What matters more is games played for counting stats. Some targets play only 10 games in our playoff weeks, some have a 2-game week, and some have back-to-backs they may sit.

In the first weeks, check minutes and usage before checking shooting. Several targets need about 30 minutes or a starting role to give the volume this build needs. If a waiver-watch guard wins a starting role at about 27 to 28 minutes, put in a FAB bid at once.
